partner_context.their_ambition: You are India's largest integrated transport utility - 15 domestic ports, 115+ marine vessels, airports (including Mumbai and the new Navi Mumbai), logistics parks and the Vizhinjam deepwater transshipment port - with a stated mission to connect India's 7,500 km coastline end-to-end.
partner_context.their_pressure: Your network is built for cargo; the passenger and coastal-mobility layer of India's coastline is wide open, unmonetized, and aligned with the government's Maritime India Vision 2030 push for modern marine transport. Owning the clean passenger surface across your port-and-airport footprint is the natural next frontier.
partner_context.where_navier_fits: Navier is the fleet and operating model that turns the Adani coastline into a passenger-mobility network: a software-defined foiling-electric fleet berthed at your ports, fed by your airports, connecting the coastal cities and islands along the footprint you already own - the same network model proven in the Maldives.

hero.title: Adani Ports x Navier - the passenger layer of India's coastline
hero.subtitle: 15 ports, airports and 7,500 km of coastline - the infrastructure backbone for India's foiling-electric mobility network.
hero.what_we_do_together: Adani provides the berths, the port-and-airport network and the coastline footprint; Navier provides the software-defined foiling-electric fleet and the Maldives-proven operating playbook. Together we stand up the clean passenger-mobility layer of India's coast - airport-to-water links, coastal city corridors and island connectivity - across the network Adani already operates.

why_now: India's Maritime India Vision 2030 is actively pushing modern marine transport across 12 major and 200+ non-major ports; Adani's Vizhinjam deepwater port and its airports (Mumbai, Navi Mumbai) are coming online; Kochi's electric Water Metro proves the clean-ferry appetite; and a ~100-vessel foiling network is ramping next door in the Maldives. The infrastructure backbone exists - it needs the fleet.
multimodal_fit: Adani already owns the hardest infrastructure - berths, ports, marine ops and airports. Navier slots a foiling-electric passenger fleet onto that backbone: land at an Adani airport, foil from the adjoining Adani berth, arrive at a coastal Adani port - a seamless air-to-water-to-shore journey across one operator's footprint.

objections.concern: Adani's network is built for cargo, not passengers.
objections.response: That is precisely the opportunity: the berths, marine ops and airports already exist; Navier adds the passenger fleet and operating model on top of infrastructure Adani already runs - no greenfield build.

objections.concern: Coastal passenger demand is unproven at scale in India.
objections.response: Mumbai's M2M ferry and water taxi, Kochi's Water Metro and the Andaman ferries all prove latent demand on diesel craft - Navier upgrades that demand with speed and clean propulsion.

objections.concern: Passenger marine licensing differs from cargo-port operations.
objections.response: State maritime boards already license the existing ferry and water-taxi services; Adani's regulatory weight and Navier's Maldives operating playbook de-risk the passenger path.

objections.concern: Why not just run conventional fast-ferries?
objections.response: Hydrofoiling is ~10x more efficient, faster, smoother and near-silent - and Pioneer II is all-electric, aligning with the clean-transport mandate Adani and the government are pursuing.

close.title: India's coastline, switched on.
close.body: From Mumbai's air-to-water link to Vizhinjam and a cross-coast Quanta-LR spine - the clean passenger layer of India's largest transport utility, foiling and berthed on the network Adani already owns.

why_navier_now.step_change: Hydrofoiling lifts the hull clear of the water, so a Navier vessel flies instead of plowing through chop - roughly 10x more efficient than a conventional planing boat, faster (30+ kt cruise), and dramatically smoother and quieter. It's software-defined and autonomy-ready, so the same fleet keeps getting better and cheaper to run over time. A step-change in marine mobility, not an incremental faster boat.
why_navier_now.no_new_infrastructure: Navier rides on infrastructure that already exists - the open ocean and the berths and jetties already in use. No vertiports, no new rights-of-way, no tunnels or tracks. Pioneer II needs only a berth pedestal; the Quanta-LR hybrid needs no charging infrastructure at all. That's the fundamental contrast with flying taxis and other new-infrastructure modes: nothing to permit, build, or wait for.
why_navier_now.the_moment: India's Maritime India Vision 2030 is pushing modern marine transport just as Adani's Vizhinjam port and airports come online, Kochi's Water Metro proves the clean-ferry appetite, and a ~100-vessel foiling network ramps next door in the Maldives. The infrastructure backbone exists - it needs the fleet.
